req.title: Create task
req.statement: The system shall create a new task and respond with HTTP 201 and the created task body when POST /tasks/ receives a valid TaskCreate payload.
expected_outcomes: response body includes id, title, completed=false

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that POST /tasks/ with a valid TaskCreate payload returns HTTP 201 and a body containing id, title, and completed=false. I designed: (1) a positive EP test with a fully valid payload asserting exact status code 201 and all response fields; (2) a negative NEG test with a missing required 'title' field asserting HTTP 422 (FastAPI validation error, not 201); (3) a BVA boundary test with title at exactly 1 character (minimum allowed by min_length=1) asserting 201 and correct echo; (4) a BVA boundary test with title at exactly 100 characters (maximum allowed by max_length=100) asserting 201; (5) a BVA boundary test with title at 101 characters (one over max) asserting 422; (6) a DT test with completed=true explicitly set asserting the field is echoed correctly (catches boolean-negation mutations on the default); (7) a NEG test with an empty string title asserting 422. Each test uses an in-process TestClient, isolated SQLite in-memory DB via dependency override, and exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_create_task_valid_payload_returns_201_with_body
preconditions: valid TaskCreate payload with title and description
actions: POST /tasks/ with {"title": "Buy milk", "description": "From the store", "completed": false}
trace: R-TASK-001: valid payload -> HTTP 201 + task body
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import Base, get_db

engine_mem = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionMem = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine_mem)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine_mem)

def override_get_db():
    db = SessionMem()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

def test_create_task_valid_payload_returns_201_with_body():
    payload = {"title": "Buy milk", "description": "From the store", "completed": False}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body["id"], int)
    assert body["title"] == "Buy milk"
    assert body["description"] == "From the store"
    assert body["completed"] is False
    assert "created_at" in body

trace: R-TASK-001: STC state transition from empty->one task->two tasks; catches id-generation mutations
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import Base, get_db

engine_mem9 = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
SessionMem9 = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine_mem9)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine_mem9)

def override_get_db9():
    db = SessionMem9()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db9
client9 = TestClient(app)

def test_create_task_response_id_is_unique_across_two_calls():
    r1 = client9.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task One"})
    assert r1.status_code == 201
    body1 = r1.json()
    r2 = client9.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Task Two"})
    assert r2.status_code == 201
    body2 = r2.json()
    assert body1["id"] != body2["id"]
    assert body1["title"] == "Task One"
    assert body2["title"] == "Task Two"
    assert body1["completed"] is False
    assert body2["completed"] is False
